You are a molecular design agent.
You may ONLY modify molecules using tools.
Only make one modification at a time.
Read the parameter descriptions for the tools very carefully.
Always ensure that your modifications don't break valence rules and do not result in a fragmented molecule.
After each successful tool call, check its result message and the updated atom table against what you intended - if it modified the wrong part of the molecule, call undo_last_change before continuing.
Every tool except crossover_molecules acts ONLY on your current working molecule (ligand 1) - none of them can see or touch the second candidate ligand. Treat ligand 2 as inspiration only: if you want to bring in one of its features, either call crossover_molecules to combine the two, or rebuild that feature yourself on your current working molecule (e.g. with add_substructure). An atom index you give to any tool other than crossover_molecules is always interpreted against your current working molecule, never against ligand 2 - do not reason about 'modifying ligand 2' and then call one of these tools, since the edit will land on the wrong molecule and likely do nothing you intended.

Ligand 1 is a benzothiazole amide on a pyrrolidinone, QED 0.688 and jnk3 0.03 - and benzothiazol-2-ylamino is a fragment I have already measured at 0.01, so there is nothing to rescue. Atom 0 is its tolyl methyl over an acyclic bond, the anchor. Having scanned the azine ring thoroughly, this episode moves to the one part of the pharmacophore I have never varied at all: the anilide linker itself. Every active molecule in two runs uses Ar-NH-C(=O)-cycloalkyl, and I have changed the cycloalkyl and found it irrelevant, but never the carbonyl. A cyclopropanesulfonamide keeps everything that I know matters - a free N-H on the ring, conjugated, with the azine linkage untouched - while replacing the planar carbonyl with a tetrahedral sulfonyl that accepts two hydrogen bonds instead of one and makes the N-H considerably more acidic. If activity survives, the linker is just a spacer and I have a whole new axis to optimise on; if it collapses, the carbonyl is part of the recognition and I should stop treating the cap as free. The surviving methyl becomes the pyridine 4-methyl. Expected product: about 303 Da.
